newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Simsmetal says 96/97 profit to fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Simsmetal says 96/97 profit to fall.

text.p: Metals recycler Simsmetal Ltd managing director John Crabb said on Friday that the poor outlook for metal prices meant profit for the year to June 30, 1997 would be lower than in 1995/96.
"It will be lower for the full year," Crabb told reporters after the group's annual meeting.
Crabb also said the group was in discussions for the acquisition of a large metals recycling business in Britian, but could not comment further because he was bound by confidentiality agreements.
He said the acquisition, if successfully completed, would be funded from cash reserves and debt issuance as Simsmetal had plenty of scope to increase its debt.
Crabb also said it was unlikely that ferrous metals prices would improve before the beginning of the new fiscal year to June 30, 1998.

"We just can't see too much hope on the immediate horizon," he said. In mid-October, Simsmetal announced its net profit for the first quarter of 1996/97 fell 34 percent to A$8.28 million. Its 1995/96 net profit had fallen 23 percent to A$46.7 million.
In October, Simsmetal said its second quarter results would be lower than in the first quarter, but did not say the full year profit would be lower.
Crabb said the construction market which used the long steel produced by electric furnaces supplied by Simsmetal remained weak and had no immediate prospect of improvement.
"Our view is that we should start to see some improvement (in ferrous metals prices) towards the end of calendar 1997, we may see it in the middle (of calendar 1997)," he said.
"We can't see too much on the horizon at this time."
The outlook for ferrous metals like copper was also very uncertain.
Pressed for more details about the acquisition, Crabb said: "It's in the U.K. For us it will be quite large," he said.
"We'll use either some cash or our unusued borrowing lines. We've got no problems funding it."
He said Simsmetal had ended the first quarter with about A$62 million cash on hand.
"I guess we'd only be using 55-60 percent of our borrowing capacity at the moment."
Simsmetal had total non-current borrowings of A$54.11 million as at June 30, 1996, giving a total warchest for possible acquisitions of about A$115 million.
Simsmetal's shares were up three cents at A$6.91 at 1.45 p.m. (0245 GMT).
